items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: To have been able to record a record with what essentially was Soprano Summit. Davern, Wilber, Haggart on bass, Dave Frishberg on piano and Bucky, and me on drums.

ctx.x: Where did Duffy Jackson fit in that timeline?

There were four white drummers in a row. From Butch, who got the gig I think in ’75 through about ’79, then Duffy for a year, then Greg Fields was there for two years and then I was there for six months, and then Dennis Mackrel was after me. In 1983 he came after me. So I’m just honored to have my name in the list of people. It doesn’t matter that I didn’t record with them or that I didn’t do any extensive touring. It was all domestic. I just missed a tour to England, I just missed a tour to Japan. It was like I…
Yeah, yeah. I know exactly what you mean. They seem to have — maybe it’s just the lives they’ve led.
